title: Temple of the Sun
visualBrief: Specific standing Ritan ritual core: mapped low square gray altar/pale coping and corner strips, four straight cardinal stair flights with splayed pale cheeks, circular low red enclosure/green tiled coping, three open west stone portals and one closed red-leaf stone portal on each other cardinal approach. Original simplified pointed finials/scroll ends and shallow stone decoration. No roofed central temple, invented altar balustrade or copied inscriptions/sculpture/mural atlas. Other park pavilions, northwest auxiliary halls, Sun Worship mural and landscaping remain separate host context, not claimed authored in this ritual-core model.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Named standard PMTiles Altar of the Sun POI35184495982750 and its central platform building35185801754351 correlate candidateQ964720. Platform four measured corners fix15.843x16.774m envelope/center[1.891951470026,-6.183890072934] and near-east-west cross axis; retain its slight mapped skew through explicit x/z vectors rather than inventing an orthogonal survey. Pedestrian courtyard35184495982750 supplies the approximately74.6m circular boundary. Native approaches35185801754350 support four cardinal portals and the west axis. Anchor116.438111111,39.914416666, heading0/native east-south axes. Circular wall/gates approximately centered on the altar, west triple facing west. Fine gate foundations lack separate footprints; radius37.3m, portal positions/open/closed assignments are picture/map approximations with about3m/5degree uncertainty, not exact-QID footprint registration.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Two ordinary pictured-state references: altar top about1.2m above its sampled upper ground envelope, nine nearby stair rises/four cardinal approaches. Enclosure red body1.55m above sampled grade plus green coping0.24m; west center stone portal4.7m, side portals4.3m, other three4.0m above their local threshold. Three west openings3.4m wide/2.65m tall; other gates3.2m wide with closed red leaves. Counts, leaf studs/scroll relief, heights and absolute threshold levels are estimates. The central altar has no roof/balustrade; old intact ceremonial interiors are not reconstructed.
